national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate projects worth 13,000 crore rupees in Chennai, Tamil Nadu today. Prime Minister will flag off the metro rail service of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around 4900 crore rupees. Mr Modi will also undertake a ride on the Chennai Metro from Porur Bypass Station to Poonamallee Bypass Station and back. The Poonamallee – Porur corridor features a unique 3.7-km double-decker structure with advanced signalling systems designed to support driverless operations. The Prime Minister will dedicate and inaugurate railway infrastructure projects worth over 750 crore rupees, including five Amrit Stations at Palani, Vellore Cantonment, Ambasamudram, Paramakudi and Namakkal, which have been redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat Station scheme. Mr Modi will perform Darshan and Pooja at the Jalakandeswarar Temple near the Porur lake. The stage is all set for the Prime Minister’s visit today at Chennai. The city has brightened up to welcome the Prime Minister as he is set to launch several projects based on infrastructure in road development , ports and innovation in sciences. This includes laying the foundation stone and inauguration of key National Highway projects to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency. The road projects will reduce the travel time apart from easing traffic congestion in National Highways in Salem, Madurai and Nagapattinam. He will also lay the foundation stone for Lube Oil Base Stocks project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited. The prime minister will also inaugurate an additional Coal Berth project and lay the foundation stone for capital dredging works for additional Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port . Mr Modi will dedicate to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras, a pioneering global scientific mission to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, across the human lifespan – from the foetal stage to old age. Prime Minister will participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya School in Chennai before leaving to Delhi.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 37 Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana completes one year today
national_raw_news.content: Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana has completed one year today. The scheme was launched on this day last year to strengthen agriculture in 100 Aspirational Agricultural Districts across the country. Our correspondent reports that the scheme has brought together 36 Central schemes across 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private sector participation, to address district-specific agricultural needs. India’s agriculture sector has significant potential across diverse regions and farming communities. Approved by the Union Cabinet in July last year, the six-year initiative was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 11th October last year. It brings together 36 Central schemes across 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private sector participation, to address district-specific agricultural needs. PMDDKY completed its first year, today marking a year of focused district-level action. Across 100 districts, District Action Plans and indicator-based monitoring are now in place. District-specific interventions are supporting agricultural development on the ground. The scheme aims to improve agricultural productivity, irrigation facilities, access to credit and post-harvest infrastructure. The Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana follows a three-tier implementation structure at the district, state and national levels. District Action Plans are prepared according to local agricultural needs, with progress monitored through one hundred twenty one indicators across 36 Central schemes. During the first year, all 100 selected districts prepared their action plans, which are under implementation. The average performance score of these districts increased from 18.85 in April 2026 to 46.89 in August 2026, reflecting improvement across all six objectives of the scheme. The initiative has also promoted knowledge-sharing among farmers. The PM-DDKY Farmer Producer Organisations Sangam, held in December 2025, brought together more than 72 Farmer Producer Organisations from 15 States and 33 scheme districts to share experiences and explore opportunities in agricultural productivity, market access and income enhancement. The progress achieved provides a foundation for stronger convergence and sustained agricultural development in the years ahead.
